sentences.text: The Royal Commission into National Natural Disaster Arrangements examined how Australia prepares for, responds to and recovers from natural disasters, and how it reduces disaster risks.
sentences.support:
These arrangements 
concern all phases of disaster management: mitigation, preparedness, response, and 
recovery.

sentences.text: It considered government responsibilities, coordination, resilience, climate adaptation and the Commonwealth’s legal role in national emergencies.
sentences.support:
whether changes are needed to Australia’s legal framework for the 
involvement of the Commonwealth in responding to national emergencies.

sentences.text: The Commission concluded that Australia needed a national approach, with greater cooperation and resource sharing while states and territories retained primary responsibility.
sentences.support: We have concluded that Australia needs a national approach to natural disasters.

sentences.text: It recommended stronger national coordination, permanent resilience and recovery arrangements, compatible emergency communications, consistent public warnings and better recovery support.
sentences.support:
A standing resilience and recovery body that can scale-up to meet the 
needs of a future disaster

findings.quote: We have concluded that Australia needs a national approach to natural disasters.

A narrow focus on response and 
recovery will leave Australia vulnerable.

notes: The overview does not state an overall recommendation total; recommendations are listed by chapter on PDF pages 34–46. State and territory responsibility is retained within the proposed national approach.
